items.title: Five Steps of Making Human Insulin

source_refs.note: The five steps of making human insulin under topic 20.5, the closing paragraph and Figure 20.8 (PDF 165-166), as printed. The exercises (PDF 166-168) are not part of the lesson body.

items: Preparation of the Two Genes: Since insulin consists of two distinct chains, scientists synthesise two different DNA sequences: one for Chain A and one for Chain B.

Construction of Recombinant Plasmids: Two sets of plasmids are obtained. The DNA for Chain A is inserted into one set of plasmids, and the DNA for Chain B is inserted into another. In both cases, the insulin gene is often attached next to a bacterial gene (like lacZ) to help the bacteria "recognize" and express the foreign DNA.

Transformation of Host Cells: The recombinant plasmids are introduced into two separate cultures of Escherichia coli bacteria. Culture 1 acts as a factory for Chain A. Culture 2 acts as a factory for Chain B.

Fermentation and Protein Expression: The bacteria are grown in large industrial bioreactors. As the bacteria multiply and perform their normal metabolic functions, they simultaneously "read" the human DNA and produce large quantities of the individual insulin chains.

Extraction and Chemical Joining: Once the chains are synthesized, the bacteria are harvested and the insulin chains are extracted and purified. In a laboratory setting, Chain A and Chain B are mixed together. They are linked by creating di-sulfide bonds (sulfur-to-sulfur bridges) between specific amino acids.

blocks.text: This final step creates the functional, three-dimensional human insulin molecule, identical to that produced by a healthy human pancreas.

blocks.alt: Four titled panels. 1. Preparation of the Two Genes: chain A (21 amino acids), chain B (30 amino acids), synthesised DNA for each chain. 2. Construction of Recombinant Plasmids: plasmids A and B cut by a restriction enzyme, DNA ligase gives recombinant plasmids (chain A) and (chain B). 3. Transformation of Host Cells: E. coli for each chain, chain A and B production, isolated chain A. 4. Fermentation and Protein Expression: purified chains, chemical joining, final active human insulin.
